title: The Dream of Nine Coins
source: The Turkish Jester, tr. George Borrow (1884)
lesson: Be thankful for the nine before you fight for the eleven.
lines: One night, Nasreddin fell asleep and had a wonderful dream. A stranger walked up and offered him nine silver coins.
Nine? said Nasreddin in the dream. Come on, make it ten!
Ten? Why not eleven! The stranger frowned. Nasreddin folded his arms. They argued, and argued, and argued.
Then the rooster crowed. Nasreddin woke up, and looked at his hand. Empty. Not one coin.
So he quickly shut his eyes, stuck out his hand, and said: Fine, fine! I'll take the nine!
He waited. And waited. Nothing. The dream was gone, and so were the coins.
Greed made him lose even what he was offered. Be thankful for the nine, before you fight for the eleven.
Next episode: Nasreddin hides from horsemen in the strangest place. Follow so you don't miss it!
